sentences.en: When John Stephan died, his family had little doubt that a lifetime of cigarette smoking was to blame.
sentences.zh: 约翰·斯蒂芬去世时，他的家人几乎毫不怀疑，罪魁祸首是他一辈子的吸烟史。

sentences.en: Then, the Nebraska Department of Health got an unusual tip.
sentences.zh: 随后，内布拉斯加州卫生部收到了一条不同寻常的线索。

sentences.en: Part one of a two-part series on the promise and the peril of vaping.
sentences.zh: 关于电子烟的希望与危险，两集系列报道的第一集。

sentences.en: It's Monday, October 28th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月28日，星期一。

sentences.en: You will see the animals on the wall.
sentences.zh: 你会看到墙上的动物。

sentences.en: So there's a rainbow trout and an antelope and a deer.
sentences.zh: 那里有一条虹鳟鱼、一只羚羊和一只鹿。

sentences.en: Above the fireplace.
sentences.zh: 在壁炉上方。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: Julie, tell me about this trip you took to Nebraska.
sentences.zh: 朱莉，跟我讲讲你去内布拉斯加州的那次旅行。

sentences.en: So, a couple of weeks ago, I went to Omaha, Nebraska.
sentences.zh: 几周前，我去了内布拉斯加州的奥马哈。

sentences.en: Julie Bosman is a national reporter at The Times.
sentences.zh: 朱莉·博斯曼是《时报》的一名全国记者。

sentences.en: And I went to the home of Kathleen Fimple, where she lives with her dog, Beau, a little terrier.
sentences.zh: 我去了凯瑟琳·芬普尔的家，她和她的小梗犬博住在一起。

sentences.en: And Kathleen showed me around her house.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳带我参观了她的房子。

sentences.en: That room's a mess, but we could pull something out of it.
sentences.zh: 那个房间很乱，但我们可以从中找出一些东西。

sentences.en: And I sat down with Kathleen and her daughter, Dulcia, and her granddaughter.
sentences.zh: 我和凯瑟琳、她的女儿杜尔西亚以及她的孙女坐在一起。

sentences.en: And they showed me something that Dulcia had made after the death of her father, John Stephan.
sentences.zh: 她们给我看了杜尔西亚在父亲约翰·斯蒂芬去世后制作的东西。

sentences.en: My daughter made this.
sentences.zh: 这是我女儿做的。

sentences.en: It was a glass box.
sentences.zh: 那是一个玻璃盒。

sentences.en: Well, that's what we used for the funeral.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是我们在葬礼上用的。

sentences.en: And inside were mementos that represented his life.
sentences.zh: 里面装满了代表他一生的纪念品。

sentences.en: He played guitar.
sentences.zh: 他会弹吉他。

sentences.en: So we've got guitar picks.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有吉他拨片。

sentences.en: And Grandma's Feather Bed was a song we all liked to sing together.
sentences.zh: 《奶奶的羽毛床》是我们大家都喜欢一起唱的一首歌。

sentences.en: So John was a very active outdoorsman.
sentences.zh: 约翰是一个非常活跃的户外运动爱好者。

sentences.en: There was a turkey feather from one of his hunting expeditions.
sentences.zh: 那里有一根他狩猎探险时留下的火鸡羽毛。

sentences.en: There's a shotgun shell.
sentences.zh: 有一个霰弹枪弹壳。

sentences.en: There's the antler.
sentences.zh: 还有那个鹿角。

sentences.en: This knife has an antler.
sentences.zh: 这把刀上有一个鹿角。

sentences.en: There were badges and pins.
sentences.zh: 还有徽章和别针。

sentences.en: He was a scout leader.
sentences.zh: 他曾是一名童子军领袖。

sentences.en: And there were dried flowers from his funeral spray.
sentences.zh: 还有他葬礼花束上的干花。

sentences.en: These are from the casket spray.
sentences.zh: 这些来自棺木上的花束。

sentences.en: And how exactly did he die?
sentences.zh: 他到底是怎么去世的？

sentences.en: So John died after a long illness.
sentences.zh: 约翰是在长期患病后去世的。

sentences.en: He was a lifelong smoker.
sentences.zh: 他是个老烟民。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: What did he smoke?
sentences.zh: 他抽什么烟？

sentences.en: Marlboros.
sentences.zh: 万宝路。

sentences.en: And not the lights, the...
sentences.zh: 不是淡味的那种，是……

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: So he started smoking back in the 60s when he was a teenager.
sentences.zh: 他从60年代十几岁时就开始抽烟了。

sentences.en: And it was a habit that he really stuck with for most of his life.
sentences.zh: 这个习惯他几乎坚持了一辈子。

sentences.en: How did he feel about his smoking?
sentences.zh: 他对自己吸烟这件事怎么看？

sentences.en: Was he like, ugh, I hate this?
sentences.zh: 他是那种觉得“哎呀，我讨厌这个”的人吗？

sentences.en: Or I love it and I don't want to quit?
sentences.zh: 还是说“我喜欢它，我不想戒掉”？

sentences.en: Or how?
sentences.zh: 还是别的什么？

sentences.en: I love it and I don't want to quit.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它，我不想戒掉。

sentences.en: And also a lot of denial, especially early, early on.
sentences.zh: 而且还有很多否认心理，尤其是在刚开始的时候。

sentences.en: Oh, my grandpa lived to be, whatever, 80-something.
sentences.zh: 哦，我爷爷活到了80多岁。

sentences.en: And he smoked.
sentences.zh: 他也抽烟。

sentences.en: So he was kind of clinging to the idea that smoking wasn't bad.
sentences.zh: 所以他一直坚持认为吸烟没什么坏处。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Eventually, I think he reconciled that, yes, smoking was bad.
sentences.zh: 最终，我想他还是接受了吸烟确实有害的事实。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And it could cause cancer.
sentences.zh: 而且它会导致癌症。

sentences.en: He tried very, very hard to quit.
sentences.zh: 他非常非常努力地想要戒烟。

sentences.en: In his 30s, when we were first married, he quit several times briefly.
sentences.zh: 在我们刚结婚的30多岁时，他曾短暂地戒过几次。

sentences.en: Sometimes he would be successful.
sentences.zh: 有时他会成功。

sentences.en: And then he started up again.
sentences.zh: 然后他又开始抽了。

sentences.en: Yeah, he'd stop for a month or two.
sentences.zh: 是的，他会停一两个月。

sentences.en: And then, yeah.
sentences.zh: 然后，嗯。

sentences.en: And his daughter, when she had her own baby daughter, she would take little pictures of the baby and, like, tuck them into his packs of cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 当他的女儿有了自己的小女儿时，她会给宝宝拍些小照片，然后把它们塞进他的烟盒里。

sentences.en: So that he would see her face every time he pulled out a cigarette.
sentences.zh: 这样他每次掏出香烟时都能看到她的脸。

sentences.en: I was like, okay,
sentences.zh: 我当时想，好吧，

sentences.en: I've tried all the little tactics.
sentences.zh: 我已经试过所有的小招数了。

sentences.en: So she tried everything she could, but his addiction to nicotine was, you know, decades strong.
sentences.zh: 所以她尽了一切努力，但他对尼古丁的依赖已经持续了几十年。

sentences.en: But then he developed COPD, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, which is a very common disease that many smokers develop.
sentences.zh: 但后来他患上了慢性阻塞性肺病（COPD），这是一种许多吸烟者都会患上的常见疾病。

sentences.en: And in his case, it gave him a very bad cough and it made it difficult to breathe at times.
sentences.zh: 就他而言，这导致他咳嗽得很厉害，有时呼吸困难。

sentences.en: We'd go to church and he'd sing a line and then he'd stop and then he'd have to pick it up later because he'd have to catch his breath in between.
sentences.zh: 我们去教堂时，他唱一句就得停下来，因为中间得喘口气，所以只能过会儿再接着唱。

sentences.en: And he used to whistle all the time.
sentences.zh: 他以前总是喜欢吹口哨。

sentences.en: He couldn't whistle anymore.
sentences.zh: 后来他再也吹不了了。

sentences.en: He had atrial fibrillation.
sentences.zh: 他患有心房颤动。

sentences.en: And sometime later, he got non-Hodgkin's lymphoma and had to have chemotherapy for years.
sentences.zh: 后来，他又得了非霍奇金淋巴瘤，不得不接受了多年的化疗。

sentences.en: I think that was when he started vaping.
sentences.zh: 我想就是那时候他开始抽电子烟的。

sentences.en: Do you know how he got the idea?
sentences.zh: 你知道他是怎么想到这个主意的吗？

sentences.en: No, we'd both.
sentences.zh: 不，我们俩都……

sentences.en: I'd kind of seen advertising.
sentences.zh: 我见过一些广告。

sentences.en: That's for it and things.
sentences.zh: 关于它的广告之类的。

sentences.en: But it was his idea and he bought one and came home with it.
sentences.zh: 但那是他自己的主意，他买了一个，然后带回了家。

sentences.en: So John started vaping about five years ago.
sentences.zh: 所以约翰大约在五年前开始抽电子烟。

sentences.en: Do you know which brand?
sentences.zh: 你知道是什么牌子吗？

sentences.en: Mystics.
sentences.zh: Mystics。

sentences.en: Then he had Blue and then he went to Juul.
sentences.zh: 后来他用过 Blue，然后换成了 Juul。

sentences.en: And he only went to Juul less than a year ago.
sentences.zh: 他换成 Juul 还不到一年。

sentences.en: And he had heard about vaping as the cleaner, healthier alternative to cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 他听说电子烟是比香烟更清洁、更健康的替代品。

sentences.en: So he became just as enthusiastic of a vaper as he was a smoker.
sentences.zh: 于是他成了电子烟的狂热拥护者，就像他曾经是个老烟民一样。

sentences.en: So earlier this year...
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候……

sentences.en: There was a cough cold going around.
sentences.zh: 当时流行一种咳嗽感冒。

sentences.en: It was a cold winter and everybody had a cold and a cough and John kind of got it the worSt.
sentences.zh: 那是一个寒冷的冬天，每个人都感冒咳嗽，约翰的情况似乎最严重。

sentences.en: And it probably, in some ways, was less obvious to us because he had a smoker's cough.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我们可能没那么在意，因为他本来就有吸烟者的咳嗽。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he coughed.
sentences.zh: 所以他咳嗽了。

sentences.en: But it was also obvious that this was worse.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，这次情况更糟。

sentences.en: And his daughter, Dulcia, started nagging at him and saying,
sentences.zh: 他的女儿杜尔西亚开始唠叨他，说：

sentences.en: Dad, you really need to go to the doctor.
sentences.zh: 爸爸，你真的需要去看医生。

sentences.en: That's probably why he went, though, in April.
sentences.zh: 这可能就是他四月份去医院的原因。

sentences.en: Because you kept pushing him.
sentences.zh: 因为你一直在催他。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he did.
sentences.zh: 所以他去了。

sentences.en: And he was diagnosed with pneumonia.
sentences.zh: 他被诊断出患有肺炎。

sentences.en: Dr. Simon said, you have pneumonia, you're going to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 西蒙医生说，你得了肺炎，必须住院。

sentences.en: And he was in the hospital for a week.
sentences.zh: 他在医院住了一周。

sentences.en: And seven, eight days into his hospital stay.
sentences.zh: 在住院的第七、八天。

sentences.en: His hands were like ice.
sentences.zh: 他的手像冰一样凉。

sentences.en: They were starting to turn blue.
sentences.zh: 它们开始变蓝了。

sentences.en: He couldn't blink.
sentences.zh: 他无法眨眼。

sentences.en: And his mouth was propped open.
sentences.zh: 嘴巴也张着合不上。

sentences.en: And he wasn't breathing very often.
sentences.zh: 呼吸频率也很低。

sentences.en: And his last breath, I could tell because there was just a slight twitch in his neck.
sentences.zh: 我能感觉到他最后一口气，因为他的脖子微微抽动了一下。

sentences.en: He died of acute respiratory failure, which the doctor said was a consequence of the COPD.
sentences.zh: 他死于急性呼吸衰竭，医生说这是慢性阻塞性肺病的后果。

sentences.en: So essentially, he died of smoking or a smoking-related lung disease, it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，听起来他是死于吸烟或与吸烟相关的肺部疾病。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: His wife said that he always believed that he was going to die of lung cancer.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子说，他一直认为自己会死于肺癌。

sentences.en: So when the doctors said that he had died essentially as a consequence of COPD, they had no reason to question the doctor's conclusion.
sentences.zh: 所以当医生说他本质上是死于慢性阻塞性肺病的后果时，他们没有理由质疑医生的结论。

sentences.en: And as tragic as that is, it all kind of lines up with our understanding of what a lifetime of smoking does to a person.
sentences.zh: 尽管这很悲剧，但这与我们对长期吸烟对一个人造成的影响的理解是一致的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But then four months after John died, Kathleen was sitting at work one day.
sentences.zh: 但在约翰去世四个月后，凯瑟琳有一天在上班时。

sentences.en: I was in a meeting when the Department of Health called.
sentences.zh: 我正在开会时，卫生部打来了电话。

sentences.en: She got a phone call from an investigator at the Nebraska Department of Health.
sentences.zh: 她接到了内布拉斯加州卫生部一名调查员的电话。

sentences.en: And he asked her all kinds of questions.
sentences.zh: 他问了她各种各样的问题。

sentences.en: He asked about any exposure in the past to, like, moldy wood or wood chips, to asbestos, to pesticides.
sentences.zh: 他询问了过去是否接触过发霉的木头、木屑、石棉或杀虫剂等。

sentences.en: Then they asked about symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 然后他们询问了症状。

sentences.en: He asked if he had had any kind of vomiting before his death.
sentences.zh: 他问他在去世前是否有过呕吐。

sentences.en: Did he lose weight?
sentences.zh: 他体重减轻了吗？

sentences.en: Was he coughing?
sentences.zh: 他在咳嗽吗？

sentences.en: And he also asked her about vaping.
sentences.zh: 他还问了她关于电子烟的事。

sentences.en: I said, I don't know why vaping.
sentences.zh: 我说，我不知道为什么要问电子烟。

sentences.en: I mean, yes, he vaped.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，是的，他抽电子烟。

sentences.en: But I don't think it's from vaping.
sentences.zh: 但我不认为是因为电子烟。

sentences.en: They said he had pneumonia.
sentences.zh: 他们说他得了肺炎。

sentences.en: Lifelong smoker.
sentences.zh: 一辈子的烟民。

sentences.en: COPD.
sentences.zh: 慢性阻塞性肺病。

sentences.en: And the investigator got off the phone with her and said he would be in touch.
sentences.zh: 调查员挂断电话后告诉她，他会再联系她。

sentences.en: So, Julie, what was John's relationship to vaping?
sentences.zh: 那么，朱莉，约翰和电子烟之间是什么关系？

sentences.en: Kathleen told me that when he was smoking cigarettes, he would smoke a cigarette two or three times an hour.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳告诉我，当他抽香烟时，他每小时会抽两到三次。

sentences.en: And very quickly, he was vaping two or three times an hour.
sentences.zh: 很快，他每小时就要抽两三次电子烟。

sentences.en: It was a straight replacement for cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 这完全是为了替代香烟。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Part of it was habit.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是习惯使然。

sentences.en: You know, years and years of habit.
sentences.zh: 你知道，多年的习惯了。

sentences.en: When you get in the vehicle, you light up a cigarette.
sentences.zh: 当你坐进车里，就会点上一根烟。

sentences.en: So when he'd get in the vehicle and start to drive, he would vape.
sentences.zh: 所以当他坐进车里开始开车时，他就会抽电子烟。

sentences.en: It was a good way to, you know, help him get his nicotine fix.
sentences.zh: 这对他来说是个不错的方法，你知道，能帮他缓解尼古丁瘾。

sentences.en: I knew it wasn't the perfect solution.
sentences.zh: 我知道这不是完美的解决方案。

sentences.en: But again, figured it was better.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，我觉得这总比抽烟好。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: For him and for us.
sentences.zh: 对他和我们来说都是。

sentences.en: Did you ever think, like, could they be dangerous?
sentences.zh: 你有没有想过，比如，它们会不会有危险？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: You know, when they first marketed him, they said it was a safer alternative.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当它们刚开始推向市场时，都说是更安全的替代品。

sentences.en: We assumed it was healthier for those around him as well.
sentences.zh: 我们以为这对身边的人也更健康。

sentences.en: And then a few days later, Kathleen spoke to the medical investigator again.
sentences.zh: 几天后，凯瑟琳再次与法医调查员进行了交谈。

sentences.en: And he told her that it had been confirmed John was Nebraska's first official vaping-related death.
sentences.zh: 他告诉她，已经确认约翰是内布拉斯加州首例官方认定的电子烟相关死亡病例。

sentences.en: This morning, Nebraska health officials have announced the state's first vaping-related death.
sentences.zh: 今天早上，内布拉斯加州卫生官员宣布了该州首例与电子烟相关的死亡病例。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The person was over 65 and from the Douglas County, which is the Omaha area.
sentences.zh: 死者年龄超过65岁，来自奥马哈地区的道格拉斯县。

sentences.en: The individual died in May, but the state health department just identified it as vaping-related.
sentences.zh: 此人于五月去世，但州卫生部门最近才将其认定为与电子烟有关。

sentences.en: So, Julie, what exactly is going on here?
sentences.zh: 那么，朱莉，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Why is an original conclusion about John's cause of death now being re-evaluated and it seems challenged?
sentences.zh: 为什么关于约翰死因的最初结论现在被重新评估，而且似乎受到了质疑？

sentences.en: What is happening?
sentences.zh: 到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: So, back in May when John died, there really was no such thing as a vaping-related death or a vaping-related illness.
sentences.zh: 五月份约翰去世时，实际上还没有“电子烟相关死亡”或“电子烟相关疾病”这种说法。

sentences.en: But throughout the summer, all these illnesses and deaths began to be reported.
sentences.zh: 但整个夏天，这类疾病和死亡病例开始不断被报道。

sentences.en: And all over the country, people began to look back at cases of people who had died, people who had gotten sick, and started to think a little differently about them.
sentences.zh: 全国各地的人们开始回顾那些已经去世或患病的人的病例，并开始以不同的眼光看待它们。

sentences.en: And in Nebraska, the state health department wouldn't have even looked at John's death if they hadn't received a tip.
sentences.zh: 而在内布拉斯加州，如果不是收到举报，州卫生部门甚至不会去调查约翰的死因。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能读到什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Julie, tell me about this tip.
sentences.zh: 那么，朱莉，跟我说说这个举报吧。

sentences.en: So, here's what happened.
sentences.zh: 事情是这样的。

sentences.en: John had an old friend who he went to high school with, and they saw each other at an alumni reunion a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 约翰有一位高中老同学，几年前他们在校友聚会上见过面。

sentences.en: They sat together with their spouses at this dinner, and throughout the dinner, as she described it, John was vaping constantly.
sentences.zh: 他们和各自的配偶坐在一起吃饭，据她描述，整个晚餐期间，约翰一直在抽电子烟。

sentences.en: And she had never seen anyone vape before.
sentences.zh: 而且她以前从没见过有人抽电子烟。

sentences.en: This was in 2014.
It was kind of a new thing.
sentences.zh: 那算是个新鲜事物。

sentences.en: And she told me that she was very alarmed by what she saw.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，她对所见到的景象感到非常不安。

sentences.en: What exactly alarmed her?
sentences.zh: 她到底为什么感到不安？

sentences.en: She was concerned because he was vaping so frequently.
sentences.zh: 她很担心，因为他抽得太频繁了。

sentences.en: Of course, when you smoke, you generally have to go outside and do it.
sentences.zh: 当然，抽传统香烟的话，通常得去外面抽。

sentences.en: But John was vaping indoors, sitting at dinner.
sentences.zh: 但约翰是在室内，坐在餐桌旁抽电子烟。

sentences.en: And she also just had this kind of gut sense that there was something kind of wrong about it.
sentences.zh: 而且她当时有一种直觉，觉得这事儿有点不对劲。

sentences.en: And she couldn't quite shake the feeling, even after the reunion was over and years had gone by.
sentences.zh: 即使聚会结束，多年过去，她也无法摆脱这种感觉。

sentences.en: And she and John really didn't keep in touch.
sentences.zh: 她和约翰其实并没有保持联系。

sentences.en: But earlier this year, when John was sick, she had heard that he was in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 但今年早些时候，约翰生病时，她听说他住院了。

sentences.en: And then she heard that he died in May.
sentences.zh: 后来又听说他在五月份去世了。

sentences.en: So she waited all summer.
sentences.zh: 于是她整个夏天都在等待。

sentences.en: And she started seeing things in the news about people getting sick and dying from vaping.
sentences.zh: 她开始在新闻里看到关于人们因抽电子烟而患病和死亡的报道。

sentences.en: There is breaking news tonight in the nationwide vaping crisis, another death, and new reports of possible lung disease.
sentences.zh: 今晚关于全国性电子烟危机的突发新闻：又有一人死亡，并有新的肺病病例报告。

sentences.en: The CDC is looking into dozens of cases.
sentences.zh: 疾控中心正在调查数十起病例。

sentences.en: The CDC can confirm 31 cases.
sentences.zh: 疾控中心确认了31起病例。

sentences.en: 200 potential cases.
sentences.zh: 200起潜在病例。

sentences.en: 380 cases.
sentences.zh: 380起病例。

sentences.en: The 450 cases.
sentences.zh: 450起病例。

sentences.en: 530 cases.
sentences.zh: 530起病例。

sentences.en: It's unclear just what's causing the problem.
sentences.zh: 目前还不清楚是什么导致了这个问题。

sentences.en: The CDC says it will continue to investigate.
sentences.zh: 疾控中心表示将继续调查。

sentences.en: And she told me that she kept looking in the paper.
sentences.zh: 她告诉我，她一直在看报纸。

sentences.en: She kept looking on the news to see if John was one of those people.
sentences.zh: 她一直在关注新闻，想看看约翰是不是其中之一。

sentences.en: And that never happened.
sentences.zh: 但一直没有相关报道。

sentences.en: So at the end of the summer, she decided that she just couldn't get rid of this feeling that vaping was related to his death.
sentences.zh: 所以夏天结束时，她决定，她无法摆脱那种“电子烟与他的死有关”的感觉。

sentences.en: So she called the state health department.
sentences.zh: 于是她给州卫生部门打了电话。

sentences.en: So she was the tip.
sentences.zh: 所以举报人是她？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So her tip gets passed along to a medical investigator.
sentences.zh: 她的举报被转交给了法医调查员。

sentences.en: And he was the investigator who called John's wife and spoke to her and interviewed her about his medical history.
sentences.zh: 就是那位调查员给约翰的妻子打了电话，采访了她关于约翰的病史。

sentences.en: He did a bunch of other things, too.
sentences.zh: 他还做了很多其他工作。

sentences.en: So he spoke to the physicians who attended to John, who treated him when he was sick in the hospital in Omaha.
sentences.zh: 他采访了约翰生前在奥马哈住院时的主治医生。

sentences.en: He examined his medical records.
sentences.zh: 他检查了约翰的医疗记录。

sentences.en: He looked at his chest x-rays.
sentences.zh: 他查看了约翰的胸部X光片。

sentences.en: And it showed pneumonia in the lower lobe of one lung.
sentences.zh: 片子显示其中一个肺的下叶有肺炎。

sentences.en: But the rest of his lungs, both sides and upper and lower, were filled with what they call ground glass opacity.
sentences.zh: 但肺部的其余部分，包括双侧的上叶和下叶，都充满了所谓的“磨玻璃影”。

sentences.en: A ground glass appearance on the lungs is an injury to the lung that is typically consistent with vaping.
sentences.zh: 肺部的磨玻璃影是一种肺部损伤，通常与电子烟有关。

sentences.en: And in some cases, it can look like there are kind of opaque white spots on the x-ray.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，X光片上看起来会有一些不透明的白点。

sentences.en: And I said, well, how does that, is that different from just a long-term smoker?
sentences.zh: 我问，这和长期吸烟者有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: And he said, yes, this is not what you would see in just routine, if you will, long-term smoking.
sentences.zh: 他说，是的，这和你所说的常规长期吸烟所看到的表现不同。

sentences.en: And in this case, it was a very key piece of evidence for the investigator who was looking into John's death.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，这对调查约翰死因的调查员来说是一个非常关键的证据。

sentences.en: And what's the understanding of how vaping might create this kind of ground glass-looking damage in the lung?
sentences.zh: 那么，人们对于电子烟如何导致这种肺部磨玻璃样损伤有什么了解吗？

sentences.en: So when you vape, of course, you use a device that heats liquid to a very high temperature and turns it into a vapor that you inhale.
sentences.zh: 当你抽电子烟时，你使用的是一种将液体加热到极高温度，并将其转化为你吸入的蒸汽的设备。

sentences.en: Now, that liquid can contain THC, which is the ingredient in marijuana that gets you high, or it could contain nicotine.
sentences.zh: 这种液体可能含有四氢大麻酚（THC），即大麻中让人产生快感的成分，也可能含有尼古丁。

sentences.en: And doctors who are investigating all these illnesses and deaths don't know exactly what it is about vaping that is making people sick.
sentences.zh: 正在调查所有这些疾病和死亡病例的医生们，并不确切知道电子烟的什么成分导致了人们生病。

sentences.en: But they have noticed that some of the people who have gotten sick or died have had the ground glass appearance on their lungs.
sentences.zh: 但他们注意到，一些患病或死亡的人，肺部都有磨玻璃影。

sentences.en: Or in some cases, they've had damage on their lungs that resembles a chemical burn.
sentences.zh: 或者在某些情况下，他们的肺部损伤看起来像化学灼伤。

sentences.en: Julie, my sense is that most of these vaping-related illnesses and the deaths that we have been reading about have been not from the well-known e-cigarette brands,
sentences.zh: 朱莉，我的感觉是，我们读到的这些电子烟相关疾病和死亡病例，大多不是来自知名的电子烟品牌，

sentences.en: but from basically counterfeit and bootleg products, right?
sentences.zh: 而是来自仿冒品和非法产品，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So here's what we know about that.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，我们了解的情况如下。

sentences.en: Of the people who have gotten sick or died from vaping in the last year, about three-quarters of them have vaped THC products.
sentences.zh: 在过去一年中因抽电子烟而患病或死亡的人中，约四分之三的人抽过THC产品。

sentences.en: A little over half have vaped nicotine, and a lot of people do both, kind of toggle back and forth between vaping weed and vaping nicotine.
sentences.zh: 略多于一半的人抽过尼古丁，很多人两者都抽，在抽大麻和抽尼古丁之间来回切换。

sentences.en: But as best we can tell, John did not vape THC.
sentences.zh: 但据我们所知，约翰并没有抽过THC。

sentences.en: When I asked his family, they kind of laughed at the idea that their 68-year-old husband and father would be procuring bootleg THC.
sentences.zh: 当我问他的家人时，他们对“他们68岁的丈夫和父亲会去买非法THC”这种想法感到好笑。

sentences.en: Is that unthinkable?
sentences.zh: 那是不可能的吗？

sentences.en: Do you have any—I mean, is that something that he might have possibly done?
sentences.zh: 你有没有——我是说，那有没有可能是他可能做过的事？

sentences.en: I don't think he would have even known where to go to get it.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他甚至知道去哪里买。

sentences.en: We've been to Colorado since it was legalized, and he wouldn't touch it.
sentences.zh: 自从科罗拉多州大麻合法化后，我们去过那里，但他碰都不碰。

sentences.en: He was never interested.
sentences.zh: 他从来没兴趣。

sentences.en: No, so I don't think he would have ever considered getting it black market either.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不认为他会考虑去黑市买。

sentences.en: They described his vaping habits as very above board.
sentences.zh: 他们形容他的电子烟习惯非常正规。

sentences.en: Do you know where he bought it?
sentences.zh: 你知道他在哪儿买的吗？

sentences.en: Walmart.
sentences.zh: 沃尔玛。

sentences.en: Uh-huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Walgreens or Walmart.
sentences.zh: 沃尔格林或沃尔玛。

sentences.en: Walgreens or Walmart.
sentences.zh: 沃尔格林或沃尔玛。

sentences.en: Uh-huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I don't think he bought it anyplace else.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他在其他地方买过。

sentences.en: He never went to any of, like, the vape shops or anything.
sentences.zh: 他从不去什么电子烟专卖店之类的。

sentences.en: Oh, never.
sentences.zh: 哦，从来不去。

sentences.en: Never.
sentences.zh: 从来没有。

sentences.en: I mean, is it possible that John was vaping something like THC, but just didn't tell his family that no one knew?
sentences.zh: 我是说，有没有可能约翰抽过类似THC的东西，只是没告诉家人，没人知道？

sentences.en: His family very strongly discounts that possibility.
sentences.zh: 他的家人非常坚决地排除了这种可能性。

sentences.en: He would have had to be doing it in secret, and they thought that that notion was rather ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 如果他真的抽过，那一定是背着人做的，而他们认为这种想法相当荒谬。

sentences.en: So if he got sick from vaping, it was from regular old—I guess if the industry's old enough to call it this—but traditional vaping.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他是因为抽电子烟而生病，那也是因为普通的——我想如果这个行业已经存在够久的话——传统的电子烟。

sentences.en: Yes, and this really only deepens the medical mystery surrounding vaping, because so many people who have gotten sick or died from vaping have been using THC vapes,
sentences.zh: 是的，这只会加深围绕电子烟的医学谜团，因为许多因抽电子烟而患病或死亡的人都在使用THC电子烟，

sentences.en: and especially vaping devices or cartridges that were bought off the street.
sentences.zh: 尤其是从街头买来的电子烟设备或烟弹。

sentences.en: And no one really knows where they came from.
sentences.zh: 没人知道它们是从哪儿来的。

sentences.en: But that's not the case with John.
sentences.zh: 但约翰的情况并非如此。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So, Julie, how does John's death, as defined and diagnosed by these medical professionals locally and nationally,
sentences.zh: 那么，朱莉，约翰的死，按照当地和全国医疗专家的定义和诊断，

sentences.en: how does it change our understanding of vaping and its consequences?
sentences.zh: 它如何改变了我们对电子烟及其后果的理解？

sentences.en: I think that his death raises an alarming possibility, and that is that someone who apparently did not vape THC, did not buy any kind of products on the black market,
sentences.zh: 我认为他的死提出了一个令人担忧的可能性，那就是一个显然没有抽过THC、没有在黑市购买任何产品的人，

sentences.en: could also become very sick and die from a vaping-related illness.
sentences.zh: 也可能因电子烟相关疾病而病重甚至死亡。

sentences.en: Right, and his family told you that he took up vaping, as many people do, because he thought it was actually going to make him healthier, it was going to help him quit smoking.
sentences.zh: 对，他的家人告诉你，他开始抽电子烟，就像许多人一样，是因为他认为这实际上会让他更健康，能帮他戒烟。

sentences.en: Yeah, he thought that this would be the thing that would help him quit smoking for good, and it did.
sentences.zh: 是的，他认为这能帮他彻底戒烟，确实也做到了。

sentences.en: And, you know, people like John Steffen are exactly the kind of person that e-cigarettes were ostensibly created for.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，像约翰·斯特芬这样的人，正是电子烟表面上所针对的目标群体。

sentences.en: When e-cigarettes were invented and when companies started selling them on the mass market,
sentences.zh: 当电子烟被发明，当公司开始在大众市场上销售它们时，

sentences.en: they said that it was for people who wanted to quit smoking and wanted a healthier alternative.
sentences.zh: 他们说这是为了那些想戒烟并想要更健康替代品的人准备的。

sentences.en: And John was exactly that person.
sentences.zh: 而约翰正是那样的人。

sentences.en: So, what's the understanding of why so many people, not just John, but hundreds of people, are getting sick from this and maybe even dying from it?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于为什么这么多人——不仅仅是约翰，而是成百上千的人——因此生病甚至可能死亡，目前有什么了解吗？

sentences.en: Well, I would just point to cigarette smoking and when it was first introduced.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我只想提一下香烟，看看它刚被引入时的情况。

sentences.en: Cigarette smoking really took off during World War I among American men.
sentences.zh: 香烟是在第一次世界大战期间在美国男性中真正流行起来的。

sentences.en: And it wasn't until the 1930s when doctors began to link an increase in lung cancer rates to an increase in cigarette smoking.
sentences.zh: 直到20世纪30年代，医生才开始将肺癌发病率的上升与吸烟的增加联系起来。

sentences.en: And it took decades after that.
sentences.zh: 那之后又过了几十年。

sentences.en: It wasn't until 1964 when the Surgeon General released a landmark report saying, yes, smoking does cause lung cancer.
sentences.zh: 直到1964年，美国卫生局局长才发布了一份具有里程碑意义的报告，称：是的，吸烟确实会导致肺癌。

sentences.en: So, I think what a lot of doctors out there are saying is that it is far too early to know what the long-term effects of vaping might be.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为很多医生都在说，现在断定电子烟的长期影响还为时过早。

sentences.en: In other words, the gestation period for any kind of public health problem is long, is maybe even decades.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，任何公共卫生问题的潜伏期都很长，甚至可能长达几十年。

sentences.en: Yes, and it's very early in e-cigarettes life.
sentences.zh: 是的，电子烟的生命周期还很短。

sentences.en: I mean, they really didn't enter the mainstream until the last 10 years.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它们真正进入主流市场也就是过去10年的事。

sentences.en: In which case, we would be at the beginning of whatever this is, not even the middle and definitely nowhere near the end.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，我们正处于这一切的开端，甚至还没到中期，更谈不上接近尾声。

sentences.en: I think we can say for sure that the CDC believes that there are many, many more cases coming and that this is only the tip of the iceberg.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们可以肯定地说，疾控中心相信未来还会有更多的病例，这仅仅是冰山一角。

sentences.en: Julie, does John's family think that he would still be alive today if he hadn't taken up vaping?
sentences.zh: 朱莉，约翰的家人认为，如果他没有开始抽电子烟，他今天还会活着吗？

sentences.en: That's a difficult question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很难回答的问题。

sentences.en: It's something that they do think about.
sentences.zh: 这是他们确实会去思考的事情。

sentences.en: And when they look back on his life, they know that taking up smoking as a teenager was certainly a bad decision.
sentences.zh: 当他们回首他的一生时，他们知道他在青少年时期开始吸烟绝对是一个错误的决定。

sentences.en: And continuing to smoke all those decades was something that they wish he had not done.
sentences.zh: 而几十年来一直持续吸烟，也是他们希望他当初没有做过的事。

sentences.en: But they thought that he made a really good decision when he switched to vaping.
sentences.zh: 但他们认为他改用电子烟是一个非常正确的决定。

sentences.en: They didn't worry about the health consequences of vaping.
sentences.zh: 他们并不担心电子烟带来的健康后果。

sentences.en: And when his daughter looked at the vaping container that was left over, sitting on the coffee table,
sentences.zh: 当他的女儿看着桌上留下的电子烟容器时，

sentences.en: she doesn't see something that is harmless or something that might have helped prolong his life.
sentences.zh: 她看到的并不是什么无害的东西，也不是什么可能有助于延长他生命的东西。

sentences.en: She sees something very dangerous.
sentences.zh: 她看到的是非常危险的东西。

sentences.en: To think that that box right there could be the sole reason he's dead, in some ways, is like looking at a gun with a bullet.
sentences.zh: 想到那个盒子可能就是他死亡的唯一原因，在某种程度上，就像看着一把装了子弹的枪一样。

sentences.en: It's just a method of death.
sentences.zh: 那只是一种死亡的工具。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Last night, the United States brought the world's number one terrorist leader to justice.
sentences.zh: 昨晚，美国将世界头号恐怖分子头目绳之以法。

sentences.en: Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi is dead.
sentences.zh: 阿布·贝克尔·巴格达迪已经死了。

sentences.en: On Sunday, President Trump announced that the founder and leader of the Islamic State died during a U.S.
sentences.zh: 周日，特朗普总统宣布，这位“伊斯兰国”的创始人和领导人在美国的一次

sentences.en: military operation in Syria.
sentences.zh: 军事行动中在叙利亚身亡。

sentences.en: Capturing or killing Baghdadi has been the top national security priority of my administration.
sentences.zh: 抓获或击毙巴格达迪一直是我政府的首要国家安全任务。

sentences.en: Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi inspired thousands of men and women from across the world to join ISIS and, in 2014, created a caliphate for the terrorist group that, at its height,
sentences.zh: 阿布·贝克尔·巴格达迪曾鼓动全球成千上万的男女加入“伊斯兰国”，并于2014年为该恐怖组织建立了一个哈里发国，在其鼎盛时期，

sentences.en: was the size of Britain and imposed a brutal form of Islam on its inhabitants.
sentences.zh: 其领土面积相当于英国大小，并对其居民实施了残酷的伊斯兰统治。

sentences.en: The thug who tried so hard to intimidate others spent his last moments in utter fear, in total panic and dread, terrified of the American forces bearing down on him.
sentences.zh: 这个曾经极力恐吓他人的暴徒，在生命的最后时刻陷入了极度的恐惧、彻底的惊慌和战栗，被逼近的美军吓得魂飞魄散。

sentences.en: After years of eluding American forces, al-Baghdadi was recently discovered in northwest Syria, where U.S.
sentences.zh: 在躲避美军多年后，巴格达迪最近在叙利亚西北部被发现，美国

sentences.en: commandos chased him into a tunnel.
sentences.zh: 突击队员将他追赶进了一条隧道。

sentences.en: There, he detonated a suicide vest that killed himself and three of his young children.
sentences.zh: 在那里，他引爆了自杀式背心，炸死了自己和三个年幼的孩子。

sentences.en: He was a sick and depraved man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个病态且堕落的人。

sentences.en: And now he's gone.
sentences.zh: 现在他已经死了。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Bavaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴瓦罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱且有时令人兴奋的斗争之中。
